titulo: If You Hear a Baby Crying Outside at Night, Don't Open the Door 🦉 #Shorts
titulo_pt: Se ouvir um bebê chorando lá fora à noite, não abra a porta
resumo_pt: Lenda da Lechuza, do norte do México e do sul do Texas: uma bruxa que vira coruja gigante com rosto de mulher. Ela imita choro e assobio para fazer você sair. O narrador assobiou de volta quando era criança.
descricao:
In northern Mexico and South Texas, grandmothers have one rule: never whistle back.

Follow @VeilFrequency for a new horror story every day. Based on Mexican folklore. Images are AI-generated.
personagens: the narrator is a Mexican-American boy of twelve in a striped t-shirt; his abuela is a small old woman with a long gray braid and a shawl; La Lechuza is a giant dark owl, taller than a man, with a pale woman's face and black eyes

scenes.text: If you ever hear a baby crying outside at night… don't open the door.
scenes.pt: Se você ouvir um bebê chorando lá fora à noite… não abra a porta.
scenes.visual: a small farmhouse door at night, a dim porch light, darkness beyond

scenes.text: In northern Mexico and South Texas, grandmothers warn about La Lechuza.
scenes.pt: No norte do México e no sul do Texas, as avós alertam sobre a Lechuza.
scenes.visual: an old grandmother with a gray braid sitting by candlelight, looking serious

scenes.text: By day, she's an old woman. At night, an owl bigger than a man.
scenes.pt: De dia, ela é uma velha. À noite, uma coruja maior que um homem.
scenes.visual: a giant dark owl perched on a fence post against the moon
the giant owl turning its head, revealing a pale woman's face with black eyes

scenes.text: She can't come in. So she makes you come out.
scenes.pt: Ela não consegue entrar. Então faz você sair.
scenes.visual: the owl's shadow on a closed window

scenes.text: First, the crying. Like a newborn, right under your window.
scenes.pt: Primeiro, o choro. Igual um recém-nascido, bem embaixo da janela.
scenes.visual: a dark bedroom window, the boy sitting up in bed listening

scenes.text: Then the whistle. Soft. Like someone calling a dog.
scenes.pt: Depois, o assobio. Baixinho. Como alguém chamando um cachorro.
scenes.visual: a dark yard at night, mist low over the grass

scenes.text: Whatever you do, don't whistle back.
scenes.pt: Faça o que fizer, não assobie de volta.
scenes.visual: the grandmother pointing a finger in warning

scenes.text: My abuela tied a rope with seven knots above our door.
scenes.pt: Minha avó amarrou uma corda com sete nós em cima da nossa porta.
scenes.visual: a rope with seven knots hanging above a wooden door

scenes.text: I was twelve. I heard the whistle. And I whistled back.
scenes.pt: Eu tinha doze anos. Ouvi o assobio. E assobiei de volta.
scenes.visual: the boy at the window with pursed lips, the dark yard outside
the farmhouse door from inside, something tall standing behind the frosted glass

scenes.text: It was my abuela's voice. But my abuela was asleep in the next room.
scenes.pt: Era a voz da minha avó. Mas a minha avó estava dormindo no quarto ao lado.
scenes.visual: the grandmother asleep in her bed, moonlight on her face

scenes.text: In the morning, there were claw marks on the door. Right above the seventh knot.
scenes.pt: De manhã, tinha marcas de garra na porta. Logo acima do sétimo nó.
scenes.visual: deep claw marks in the wood above the knotted rope, morning light

scenes.text: Abuela tied an eighth knot. She never told me why.
scenes.pt: Minha avó amarrou um oitavo nó. Nunca me disse por quê.
scenes.visual: the grandmother's hands tying an eighth knot on the rope
